utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for the day, starting with the prosecution please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Carmela Javier, Ann Sutherland, Barney Thomas, and Dan Saxon for the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone. Novak Lukic and Boris Zorko appearing for Mr. Perisic today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Before we call you, Mr. Lukic, just a small housekeeping matter. An oral decision. On the 17th of February, 2010, the prosecution filed its prosecution second motion for Defence compliance with Rule 65 ter G, submitting that two of the Rule 65 ter summaries provided by the Defence were not in compliance with the rule. The Defence responded on the 19th of February by submitting two supplemental summaries in an effort to allow the trial to proceed "expeditiously." In light of the Defence provision of these two supplemental summaries, the Trial Chamber finds that the prosecution second motion of the 17th February, 2010 is moot. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence calls witness Zlatko Danilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, will you please tell us your full name, your first and last name for the record.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Zlatko Danilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 30th of April, 1970.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Danilovic, you are here in the courtroom for the first time. During our proofing sessions I told you that we would need observe certain rules when communicating, so when I put a question to you please wait a little bit before you answer, and I will do the same. So follow the cursor on the screen and when it stops you can begin answering. Do you remember when you did your regular military service?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will very briefly go through your military CV, and you will simply confirm whether what I'm saying is correct. You entered into a contract and became a soldier for the first time in May 1992 when you joined the 63rd Parachute Brigade at the corps of special units of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please move closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, could you please move closer to the microphone, the interpreters don't hear you very well. Don't sit back like that, come closer to the microphone. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This contract was terminated in September 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you became a soldier by contract again, you became a professional soldier under contract with military post 8486 in Belgrade, that is the 72nd Special Brigade at the special units corps of the Army of Yugoslavia on the 4th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you were relieved of this duty on the 30th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever again have any contact with the military in your work and life after that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have already heard testimony before this Court about the structure of the special units corps. I would like to focus, first of all, on the structure of the 72nd Special Brigade. Before that, while you were in the 63rd Parachute Brigade, did you have any specialist training?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I went through the basic and further parachute training.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 82nd Special Brigade, what did it consist of and where was its headquarters, do you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was it the 82nd or 72nd?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 72nd.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 72nd Brigade consisted of three battalions. The military police battalion, the reconnaissance sabotage battalion, and the ambush battalion. The one I was in, that was the reconnaissance sabotage battalion, that was at Pancevo, there was one in Avala, and the support ambush battalion was in Vukovine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The military police battalion, did it have any special designation?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us what battalion you were in and where the headquarters of your battalion was? Would you repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I recall now, the name of my battalion was the military police battalion for anti-terrorist action, and it was headquartered in Avala.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you describe what Avala is for Their Honours and how far it is from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Avala is a mountain, some 30 kilometres away from Belgrade. It's wooded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your battalion, what units did it consist of, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The battalion had two professional units consisting of professional soldiers, and one unit of regular conscripts maintaining the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say unit, are you referring to a company, a platoon? Can you be more precise.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: These were companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are interested in the period towards the end of 1993 and the beginning of 1994. Who was the battalion commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Aleksandar Zivkovic was the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who the company leaders were and what company you were in?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The leader of the 1st Company was Captain Vujinovic; I was in the 2nd Company; Captain Berko Alimpic was the company leader. Later on he was replaced by Goran Galjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the third company, the one consisting of conscripts, can you recall the name of the company leader?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the name Kapor mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And your company, what units did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: It consisted of three platoons, and there were platoon leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who the leader of your platoon was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My platoon commander was Zlatic. He was a lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move into private session for a few minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many members did your battalion at Avala have?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Never more than 50 or 60 men [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if you include the officers?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Up to 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] He said, Your Honour, beginning at line 7 -- in row 7, line 11 -- line 6, 50 or 60 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This barracks at Avala, how large was it? Were there other units there as well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The barracks was quite small. It consisted of two bungalows, one where we professional soldiers were accommodated and another where the conscripts were, there was a canteen, a kitchen, and some garages for vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were at Avala, where did you have your training, for your specialist training?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the training was in the barracks or around it, but we also went Bubanj Potok where there was a training ground and where there was a shooting range and where we had tactical training.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far is Bubanj Potok from Avala?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: About 15 kilometres more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have any training in Nis and on what occasion? When you were part of the 72nd Special Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did go to Nis for parachute training.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you went to Nis for parachute training, what about the officers from Avala, did they go with you, or did they remain at Avala?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, all the members of the unit were the private officers attended the parachute training.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that period of time, or rather, throughout the whole time you spent in the 72nd Special Brigade, did you ever see General Perisic? Did he ever visit your unit?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that General Perisic visited your unit? Did you ever hear it from a colleague or an officer?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When an officer, a high-ranking officer visited your unit, what did you do? What was the procedure?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: When Stupar visited, the unit would line up and he would come out in front of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was Colonel Stupar? What was his post? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the brigade headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The brigade headquarters at the time was in Pancevo, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we are going to move on to the events that we are interested in. Do you remember December 1993 by anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where you were, or rather, let me start this way: During that month, did you train anywhere apart from Avala?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: We were at Nis at parachute training.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what happened when you returned, or rather, when did you return roughly and could you tell us what happened then?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in mid-December, that's when we returned. When we returned we were told that we would be going out into the field. At that time we didn't know where we would be going.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who told you that you would be going out into the field, do you remember, roughly?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Usually it was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you told whether you would be leaving immediately or the following day or within five days?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us, were you told where it was that you were going?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Beforehand when you went somewhere, training or out into the field, were you told where you would be going?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At one point in time, did you understand where it was that you were going, and if so, on which basis?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Just as we were about to leave, we understood because we were given live ammunition, that indicated that we would be going somewhere where there was combat.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone, we can barely hear him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, you are sitting far from the microphone, you are asked to please get closer to the microphone because the interpreters can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were all the members of your company ordered to go on that assignment?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened? How did things actually develop?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: We were told that everyone who felt unfit in any way or unable to go in any way would not have to go and would not suffer any consequences on account of that. So whoever wanted to go went.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that the unit had about 100 men, I'm referring to the entire battalion. In your view how many people from your battalion went out on that mission?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: About 50 soldiers and officers, rather NCOs. Perhaps a bit more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say soldiers, what was the status of these soldiers who left?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: All of them were professionals, that is to say, soldiers who had signed contracts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those who did not go, do you know whether later on they suffered any consequences on account of that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. All of them worked normally as they did before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Danilovic, can you tell us roughly how big your salary was at the time in December 1993? Do you remember that in any way, what you did with your salary at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we received our salary in two parts. The first part we would usually receive on the 15th, as we did then. I received money for which I could buy about 20 German marks at the time. I took that money with me, and I kept it. There was a very high inflation running at the time, and by the time I was back it was worthless. I still have that money at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How come you remember this? How come you remember that comparison, if I can put it that way, 20 Deutschemark?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time that is how we calculated everything, all of us, in Deutschemark. That's how I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you returned, did you get the second part of your salary, and if so what did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the second part of my salary was roughly that big too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In those days, how soon did one have to change the dinars in order to get the equivalent in Deutschemark?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: If you didn't buy the 20 Deutschemark on that particular day, by the next day it would be 10 Deutschemark, or perhaps even 5. It would be a lot less even on the very same evening of that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you were about to leave on that mission, were there any discussions going on as to whether there were any strings attached to it and whether you would not be paid if you did not go on that mission?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, we were professional soldiers, and there's no strings like that in a professional army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. You say that 50, roughly 50, perhaps a bit more than that, men went on that trip from your battalion. What about other battalions? What was the total of men who set out on that journey?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any members of other battalions there? Did you see them later?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there were some, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us now, do you know roughly when you set out in relation to your return from Nis?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately in a day or two, after we had arrived, we spent a day or two there, and then we left during the night. That is to say, that day when we received our salary, we left on that same night. It was roughly mid-December.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how you travelled?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, vehicles. 150s.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does that mean, 150s? All of us are lay people here, could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a vehicle that is a bit dated. A bit dated. A vehicle that belonged to the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me put it this way, that night, where did you end up?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Just before dawn we arrived at some barracks, that was Han Pijesak. The barracks at Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Han Pijesak is in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is not challenged in this courtroom. Did anyone tell you before that that you were crossing the border?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us one more thing, I would be interested in the following: The uniforms that you wore at the time, the special units, did they have any insignia, emblems when you went out into the field?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No. At that time the uniforms of the Army of Yugoslavia bore no emblems.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The tri-colour flag on your arm?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you were being given emblems of the Army of Republika Srpska to put on your uniforms either while you travelled or when you arrived at your destination?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more question, the uniforms of the special units that you belonged to, did they differ from the classical uniforms of the regular army? Did they have anything special about them?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. After Han Pijesak, where did you go on?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was that on the same day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The same day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember where you were put up in Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they put us up at this hotel. I can't remember its name, but it was in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How much time did you spend approximately at that hotel before going out into action?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: About ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During these ten days approximately, did you have any kind of activities, I mean, there in the field?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were there in Vogosca during those ten days, did you hear from anyone what it was that you came there for and what you were supposed to do there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, the locals told us about this hill called Zuc, and they showed it to us and they told us that that is what our mission would involve.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This hill, Zuc, could it be seen from Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "locals" -- first of all, did you have any contact with the Army of Republika Srpska at the time while you were there, during those ten days?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "locals," who did you mean? Who were these locals who told you that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to civilians, to people who lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now let us move on to what actually happened. Did anything happen? Did you go out into action? What happened?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 27th we set out, we went into action.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just before that --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The action was supposed to take place a day earlier; however, for some reason, now was it because of the bad weather or something, we didn't leave on that day but on the next day, during the night on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many of you set out approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: About 30 of us, because there was a virus going around and quite a few of us were ill, so not everyone went out on mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you ill?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say quite a few people did not go into action, you don't have to be very specific, but tell me how many approximately for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: About 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you also not go on mission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did go on mission. I was ill a few days before that, so by then I was already healthy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who led that group of yours, and what was the actual mission or task involved?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: There were two groups. I was in one of the two groups. In the other group was Lieutenant Galjak who was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the mission? What were you told?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The mission was to take a building that was still under construction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were the weather conditions like and what information did you have about the building before that? Did you have any assessments made?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Assessments were made, but all of the people who went out on reconnaissance, as I said, had been ill, so they didn't go. The weather was bad. There was some snow, a drizzle, rather, and it was foggy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: We were brought to the building by a local person. We went off the road a bit, and we did not come from the right side. Nevertheless, we found our way. We went out according to our assignment. My group had the task of taking bunkers and trenches. The other group had the task to enter the building. We accomplished our mission and the other group came across strong resistance. They let them enter the building and then they threw a hail of grenades at them. After about two hours of fighting we managed to get out. Unfortunately, we didn't manage to get our dead out as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many members of your unit got killed then, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, six men from my unit were killed. And about ten were wounded. All the dead were from the other group. There weren't any men killed from my group, but there were a few who were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you help in getting these people out? Did you personally do anything about it actively?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: You mean on that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I helped. I helped get the wounded out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In which town is this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we spoke to the witness yesterday we found on Google map something that the witness recognised, so could we have document ID 1D -- [In English] ID 1D11/0340.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you say that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Doc ID 1D11/0340.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Danilovic, do you recognise something?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be given a marker to try to mark some things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This building, as His Honour asked, how far was it from Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I think about 10 kilometres, maybe a little more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it in the direction of Zuc, the hill called Zuc?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: A little to one side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have a marker, so please mark the building we are talking about with number 1.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you put an arrow showing the direction from which your group arrived, and an arrow that the other group went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, take it one at a time. Let him first mark the building. And when he has marked the building, then ask him to show you the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is the building marked 1, which was the target of your action. Can you now put an arrow showing the direction from which you arrived and where you stopped.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: We came this way, and this is where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you still altogether in a group?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you put number A next to this dot.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, we split up into two groups as we had been told to do. My group set out in this direction, and what you can see here are all trenches and connecting trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where you said "my group," could you put a letter B there.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned trenches and connecting trenches. Can you draw a line showing where these trenches were.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: All of this. And this is a dugout here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just take it slowly. Can you put an X next to the trenches and connecting trenches.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And where you circled the dugout, can you put the letter C.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the second group?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Let me add, if it's important, everything you see here all of these are trenches and connecting trenches. There's another one here that you can't see very well connecting the building to the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you put the letter T next to those lines.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, please show me where this second group went.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The second group set out towards the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you put you a C there -- no, sorry, we already have a C. Turn it into an O, that will make it simple.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excellent. And can you mark the place where you were when you were helping the wounded and pulling them out, approximately.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Around here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can only say that the witness put a dot next to the letter B, for the record. I think that is sufficiently clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this picture, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D289. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Danilovic, do you remember the names of some of those who were killed from your unit in this action?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was when Galjak died; Ravic [phoen], the record keeper; and Private Smaletic [phoen]; Momcilovic, and Krsto Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened after this action? How long did you stay there, and were there any other actions?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: After the action we stayed there for about two days at the most, and there were no further actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did you return?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: We returned to our barracks in Avala.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume you remember the date of this event.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 27th of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the bodies of your fallen comrades?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I do. Ten or 15 days later, their bodies were returned. And later on they were buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Danilovic, how long did you remain in the 72nd Special Brigade after this event?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Until nearly the end of 1994, sometime until sometime in late October.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After returning from this action, did you go out on the ground again outside the territory of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of anyone else from your unit going out on the ground outside the territory of the FRY in this period of time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that anyone was asked or told to go on the -- outside the territory of the FRY in this period?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I think I would have known about it had such a request been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move into private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us when you left the unit, did you stay in contact with your colleagues from the unit in general?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every year on the 27th of December, on the day of that action, we have a kind of memorial service for the fallen, and then almost all the former and current members of the unit attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did any of your former colleagues whom you meet at these gatherings ever tell you that after this event he went to Bosnia again?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask but Cazinska Krajina, Tuzla, Srebrenica, Sarajevo -- I'll repeat, Cazinska Krajina, Tuzla, Srebrenica, Sarajevo. Did any of your colleagues mention he had been at any of these locations or heard of anyone going to these locations?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody said anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you that General Perisic visited the unit later on at Avala?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody told me anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now have to move into private session again, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. -- who do I call, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, thank you. If I could just have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Danilovic, my name is Barney Thomas. I'm lawyer with the prosecution. I have the opportunity now to ask you some questions about the testimony that you have just given. I only have very few questions, nevertheless your answers are important. Please listen to my question, answer only my question. And if there's anything about my questions that you don't understand, please let me know, and I will ask it another way. Okay?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: First of all, sir, you've not testified here at the Tribunal before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You've never provided any statement about these matters to any representative of the Office of the Prosecutor here?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, I never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you told us, sir, that you were relieved of your duty on the 30th of October, 1994. In fact, was your service terminated because you were found guilty of desertion?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Quite simply, I broke my contract with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Were you not found to have been absent from your unit for five consecutive days, was a decision not issued to that effect? And on the basis of that decision, was your service not terminated?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. However, that leave had been agreed upon with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, a formal decision was issued by your unit for the termination of your service, and the sole reason given for the termination of your service was that you had deserted your unit, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe that's the way it was officially, but it was done in agreement with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. I want to have a look at a document, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we can have XN 195 on the screen. Your Honours, this is, at the moment in e-court, only in B/C/S. The page that I'm interested in is, I think, page 29 in the B/C/S. I have a very draft translation of this page, a hard copy translation, but it was done yesterday, so it's not an official translation by any means. But I have a hard copy which I can provide to my learned friends and Your Honours to assist us with dealing with the B/C/S document once it is on the screen. And if I could provide that, sir, to Your Honours and my learned friends. I stand corrected, Your Honours, I see that the translation I speak of is already uploaded. The page I'm looking for is the next page, I think, in the B/C/S, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, just take a moment to read that document, please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: It is barely legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, we can have the passage that you need to read, which is -- we can enlarge it, sir, so that you can have the opportunity to see it on a bigger portion of the screen. And tell me when we need to go further down the document, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether I'm supposed to read all of it or just where it says "statement of reasons"?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just read the first paragraph of the statement of reasons will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The reason is --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause, sir. Just pause. I am sorry, don't read the document out, just read it to yourself, and I will ask you a couple of questions about it.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are you ready, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay, if we could have the English back on the screen, too, Mr. Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, we see there that this is an order terminating the professional military service, your professional military service; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Dated the 15th of October, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And we see that the reason for termination is clearly stated in the document, isn't it? "Unjustified absence from the service, uninterrupted leave for five days;" is that right? Just pause. That's what the document says, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: That is what it written in the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Sir, are you suggesting that this was not the case but an arrangement with your commander, that the documentation record that your service is terminated on the grounds of desertion? Is this your position?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: There was an agreement with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, sir, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination, Mr. Lukic

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was it that you discussed with the commander, and what was the consequence of that discussion with the commander?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, salaries in the military were rather low. I got the opportunity of getting another job, and then I asked the commander to let me go for a few days to go and see whether I could work at this other place. So that's the agreement we reached, and that's what happened. I came back afterwards, and then we terminated the contract. I am not aware of this unjustified absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the commander tell you that this kind of decision would be made, that this kind of decision would be written up?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the commander ask you nevertheless to remain in the unit when you discussed this matter with him? Did he want you to continue to be in that unit?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Thomas, I forgot to ask you, what did you want to do with that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honours, that should be tendered, please, my oversight, my apologies. MFI'd, and we will get an official English translation. The only page that needs to be tendered is that one B/C/S page that I referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I see you seem -- you look like you don't like what you are hearing. Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2914. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have a couple of questions which I'd like to ask you. The first question is the following: When you decided to join the army in 1992, were you told at the time that you may have to fight in Bosnia or outside of the Serbian territory?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: That was never mentioned. However, a professional soldier is a professional soldier who carries out all the tasks he is assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's the reason why you went there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Where? Please, I'm sorry I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You went to Bosnia, that is. What about the others who refused to go, why did not they go there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Everyone had a reason of his own. I don't know about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, that means that you had the choice; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you did not have to obey orders, there were no orders in the Yugoslav Army. The soldiers can choose if they agree, they can do something but only if they agree; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: In this case, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, I have another question. When you decided to leave the army 1994, why didn't you simply resign from your duties?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I did not resign because I did not know what awaited me at my new job. I wanted to be sure that at my new job I would have a bigger salary and that I would be able to provide for myself better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, but you did leave, so you know as a professional soldier that when you leave the army without resigning, it is tantamount to desertion.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: In this case, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And why not in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Because as I've already said, all of this was done in agreement with my commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, in the Yugoslav Army, you can have your own special tacit arrangements with your commander, you don't need to write things formally that you resign? All you have to do is pick up the phone and talk to your commander or go and see your commander and say, Look, you know, I want to go, good-bye?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No, this was an exception.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right then. I shall not insist. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Her Honour Judge Picard asked you about the men who did not go out on that mission. Was it their duty to explain why it was that they didn't want to go?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another question that stems from the last answers you gave to Judge Picard, did you consider yourself to be privileged in a way? Did the commander view you as one of his favourite soldiers? I mean, I'm not trying to bring you into a position now where you have sing your own praises, but did you have the impression at that time that the commander favoured you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO DANILOVIC
utterances.text: You cannot say that I was favoured, but the fact was that I was a bit, how shall I put this now, a bit more professional than others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No questions, sir, but a transcript issue. If I could go please to page 29, line 13. And Her Honour Judge Picard asked -- sorry, it's at line 15 on the version I'm looking at, sir, I'm sorry. Asked, "You went to Bosnia, that is." At which point Mr. Danilovic did answer yes, but that's not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Danilovic, that brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you so much for coming to testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down and travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess that's an opportune moment to take the break, can we take the break and come back at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can, but may I inform you that we can call our next witness only tomorrow because we are still working with the witness. Mr. Guy-Smith is still working with him. We had planned to have him brought in tomorrow. I didn't know what amount of time would be needed for Mr. Danilovic in court, but we are continuing with the proofing of this witness that we are going to call next. There are some extra maps, et cetera, that we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well then. In that event the matter stands adjourned to tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned. Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.19 a.m.
